@timneutkens I just checked out canary and I'm still seeing these warnings in `10.0.4-canary.3` and `5.10.0`. Is there additional information I could provide to narrow this down?
@timneutkens I have a small repro here — https://github.com/paambaati/nextjs-webpack-worker-bug-repro

I was able to workaround this by prepending `[runtime]-` to the `webpackConfig.output.hotUpdateChunkFilename` and `webpackConfig.output.hotUpdateMainFilename`. Looks like this is the "new" Webpack 5 way. Probably should not be used with Webpack 4. Not sure about Webpack 5 versions before this change.

issue.title: Web Workers are broken in Next.js 11
issue.body:
### What version of Next.js are you using?

11

### What version of Node.js are you using?

v14.16.0

### What browser are you using?

Chrome

### What operating system are you using?

Windows

### How are you deploying your application?

Vercel

### Describe the Bug

WebWorker behavior with Next.js 11 is highly volatile with several different errors occurring when importing them. ImportScripts also fails inside the workers. The project as-is worked fine with Next.js 10.2.3.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1667481/122135787-ca3a5400-ce5e-11eb-984c-dcfaa29f4464.png)


### Expected Behavior

WebWorker works as expected.

### To Reproduce

The default example for Web Workers is broken as well, shows the same issues. The importScripts can be reproduced by adding the importScripts code in the worker.
